title: Charter Blue — NeurIPS Bilingual Spotlight
description: A white-ground ML conference deck anchored by a cool cyan-blue section banner, vivid-blue numbered TOC, and hairline gray dividers — with a reserved margin slot for Hangul technical glossary entries. Institutional without being sterile; academic without being decorative.
philosophy: This template exists for the researcher who earns authority through precision, not spectacle — where the argument must land in a room of domain peers and the slides must not compete with it. It rejects mesh overlays, gradient noise, and any decorative motif that cannot justify its presence alongside a theorem or ablation table. It is built specifically for bilingual presenters who need to embed Korean technical glosses naturally without breaking English slide rhythm or signalling that the dual-language register is an afterthought. The model room is a spotlight session, not a boardroom; the standard is the published paper, not the investor pitch.
goodFor: NeurIPS / ICML / CVPR oral and spotlight talk slides
Numbered 5-to-7-item agenda breakdowns with strict section hierarchy
Bilingual Korean–English technical presentations requiring inline margin glosses
Academic seminars where terminology density demands visible anchoring devices
avoidFor: Consumer product launches requiring high visual energy and brand personality
Chart-heavy quarterly business reviews with multi-panel data grids
Talks built around full-bleed photography, video stills, or hero imagery
Audiences expecting persuasive narrative storytelling rather than structured exposition
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide opens with the composure of a peer-reviewed paper translated to room scale — dominant white negative space grounds the title in deliberate stillness, signaling rigor over spectacle. A cool cyan banner at the base injects controlled chromatic weight, anchoring speaker identity without competing with the argument above. Composition is top-weighted and airy, with visual gravity pulling the eye downward toward the affiliation and bilingual margin gloss. Avoid gradient wash, ornamental geometry, and any diagonal energy — every element must justify its presence by function alone.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid with an 8–9% outer margin on both sides; the main title occupies columns 2–10 and sits in the upper-center third of the slide, leaving substantial white space above and below it. A full-width cyan horizontal banner stripe anchors the lower quarter, housing presenter name, affiliation line, and a narrow right-aligned margin zone reserved for a Korean institution gloss or title transliteration. A single hairline gray rule separates the white title field from the cyan banner, serving as the sole decorative device. No header band; page number is suppressed on the cover.

examples.promptCore: The slide reads like a typeset conference-paper spread — white ground, zero decorative noise, authority earned through structural precision and cool blue anchoring devices. Composition is deliberately asymmetric: a dense, terminus-clear main column counterweighted by a narrow, quiet gloss margin that absorbs Hangul entries without disrupting English reading rhythm. Blue and cyan appear exclusively as functional wayfinding — section tag, rule accent, item numbering — never as ambient mood wash. Reject any gradient, texture, or motif that could not coexist with a theorem or ablation table.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid with an 8% outer margin; main body content occupies columns 1–9, structured as numbered or bulleted items separated by hairline horizontal rules that span the full content column. A narrow right-margin channel (columns 10–12) is reserved exclusively for inline Hangul technical glossary entries, each vertically aligned to its corresponding body line. A thin cyan horizontal section-identifier band sits flush at the top, above the slide title and its separating rule. Slide number anchors bottom-right, outside the content grid.
